When you type `https://www.example.com` into your browser and press Enter, a remarkable orchestration of protocols and systems unfolds across roughly 50–200 milliseconds in the best case, or several seconds under adverse conditions. For `www.example.com`, the browser first checks its own internal DNS cache (typically holding 256–1024 entries with a TTL equal to the record's TTL). A miss triggers a query to the operating system's resolver (the OS-level cache), which may in turn query a recursive resolver such as Cloudflare's `1.1.1.1` or your ISP's resolver.
